title: HelixCare Systems — Sprint 0 onboarding cadence huddle

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-20
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Romero, Priya Nair, Marcus Li, Rita Shah — from Redwood; Dana Kim, Carlos Mendes, Evelyn Ross, Omar Ruiz, Samira Patel — HelixCare

Auto-summary (auto-gen might be noisy): Kickoff of sprint zero for HelixCare onboarding; focus on pilot for triage assistant; network and security items high priority; timeline and bench marks discussed.

Topics / Agenda: 1) Goals 2) Security & networking 3) Benchmarks/metrics 4) Runbook and next steps

[00:00] Alex Romero: Hey everybody — thanks for joining, I think we have a full house from HelixCare, appreciate the time. Quick intros? we'll run through objectives and then jump into network and security since that's blocking for the pilot.

[00:22] Dana Kim: Hi all, Dana here — Head of ML at HelixCare. We're looking to stand up a triage assistant that interrupts front-line nurses workflows and suggests next steps, so low latency and privacy are big for us.

[00:35] Carlos Mendes: Carlos — CTO — high level we want to run a small pilot, validate latency/cost, then decide on dedicated capacity for prod. Also compliance is a hard requirement.

[00:50] Alex Romero: Great — that's inline with how we typically run sprint zero. Priya, do you want to cover the onboarding cadence?

[00:58] Priya Nair: Sure. We'll do a 2-week sprint zero: week one is access, sample prompt ingestion, and security review; week two is bench runs, tuning, and an internal demo. Weekly standups and a mid-week status. I'll send cadence and invite after this call.

[01:18] Marcus Li: On the SE side I'll own the benchmark runs and initial tuning. We'll use hosted Redwood API to get a baseline then show you how Dedicated/reserved pools change unit economics. There's a small chance we recommend a quantized variant if cost/throughput dictates.

[01:38] Evelyn Ross: On networking — our infra team prefers private link but we also can do VPC peering, depends on the egress. We have strict egress policy to the internet.

[01:50] Rita Shah: Noted — we can support both. Quick note tho: the Private deployment has a slightly different onboarding path, longer lead time. For sprint zero hosted is faster to iterate on.

[02:08] Omar Ruiz: Can you confirm what logs are kept? We need audit logs and key rotation info for our security team. SOC2 is table stakes.

[02:18] Alex Romero: Yes — we provide audit logs at the tenant level, and we have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys. We'll share the security pack after. Also Redwood's SOC2 and ISO attestation docs are in that pack.

[02:34] Samira Patel: We should set success metrics now — what are you thinking for this triage assistant?

[02:42] Dana Kim: For us: p95 latency target < 300ms for short prompts, and cost per session under $0.10 as a rough threshold. Also we need >85% match on our clinical intent labels for the evaluation set.

[03:00] Marcus Li: Those are doable as pilot targets on hosted depending on prompt length and batching. For the latency target we might need to tune batching and enable prefix caching. Note: our KV cache sometimes is referenced as "K V cash" in autosummaries — apologies for the auto transcript.

[03:20] Carlos Mendes: Cost-wise, if Dedicated is cheaper per-token we may move there for prod. But we need a predictable SLA. What SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?

[03:30] Alex Romero: Our Dedicated product has SLA tiers; baseline is 99.9% uptime with latency SLOs per model family. I'll attach the SLA doc. For the pilot we default to hosted with clear migration plan to Dedicated.

[03:44] Evelyn Ross: Can you cover the authentication options — SSO, SAML, RBAC?

[03:50] Rita Shah: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, per-route API keys for service accounts, and role-based controls in the console. We'll send the runbook for setting up RBAC and service principals.

[04:06] Omar Ruiz: KMS integration: can we bring our keys? HSM?

[04:10] Alex Romero: Yes — bring your own key (BYOK) via KMS integration is supported, and we can discuss HSM in private deployments.

[04:20] Samira Patel: On data residency — our compliance requires certain logs to not leave region. How do you handle that?

[04:27] Priya Nair: We can route requests to region-specific infra and restrict retention in the console. For the pilot we'll demonstrate regional routing and shorter retention windows.

[04:40] Marcus Li: Back to benchmarks — Marcus here. For the perf plan, I propose 3 runs: baseline on hosted, then with prefix cache enabled, then simulated Dedicated with larger batch sizes. We'll record p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and token cost.

[04:58] Dana Kim: Sounds good. We'll provide a representative prompt set (50-100 prompts) plus larger stress set.

[05:06] Alex Romero: Great. Any blockers on access? who will own credentials?

[05:12] Evelyn Ross: I'll own infra side, will need an allowlist IP or VPC peer details.

[05:18] Alex Romero: Evelyn we'll need your network diagram and egress rules. I'll put that in the action items.

[05:28] Carlos Mendes: How fast can you provision Dedicated test capacity if we want to try it?

[05:34] Rita Shah: Provisioning Dedicated can take 3-6 weeks depending on hardware selection and region, but for testing we can give a simulated capacity via hosted reserved pools and provide cost comparisons.

[05:48] Omar Ruiz: On encryption at rest, key rotation cadence — do you provide logs for rotation events?

[05:55] Alex Romero: Yes, KMS rotation events are surfaced in audit logs. We'll include examples in the security pack.

[06:06] Samira Patel: Curious about fallback behaviors — if Dedicated capacity runs low, how does traffic get routed?

[06:12] Marcus Li: We have smart routing. Requests can fallback to a compatible hosted variant; there's a policy layer to prefer latency or cost. We'll demo the routing policy in a technical deep dive.

[06:24] Dana Kim: Is model version pinning possible? We want to freeze a model family during validation.

[06:29] Rita Shah: Yes — you can pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts A/B, and automatic fallback.

[06:38] Carlos Mendes: About observability — token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards? That was mentioned in the deck.

[06:45] Alex Romero: Yup — Redwood Console shows token-level breakdown, per-model latency, tracing hooks. We can give you a demo account for visibility.

[06:55] Evelyn Ross: Ok, let's get practical: timeline and responsibilities?

[07:00] Priya Nair: Week of 9/21: access & security pack. Week of 9/28: benchmark runs and initial tune. Internal demo by 10/05. We'll confirm owners now.

[07:10] Alex Romero: I'll send pricing and SLA docs today. Marcus will run perf. Priya will own cadence. Evelyn provides infra. Dana provides prompt set.

[07:20] Samira Patel: On legal — procurement wants an initial MSA template. Can you drop a template?

[07:26] Alex Romero: Yes, procurement template and standard master services agreement I'll share; legal review usually takes a couple weeks.

[07:34] Omar Ruiz: We'll need to run a VPN connectivity test — do you have a test harness?

[07:40] Marcus Li: We have a connectivity checklist and small test endpoints. We'll coordinate with Evelyn.

[07:48] Carlos Mendes: Does Redwood provide a staging environment for mock traffic? We want to test with synthetic load.

[07:54] Rita Shah: We can create a staging tenant tied to your account for load tests; that will be separate from production.

[08:03] Dana Kim: Great — also curious about eval tooling — can we hook our internal evals to your quality monitoring?

[08:10] Marcus Li: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets. We'll show how to wire your eval harness later.

[08:18] Priya Nair: Quick note, we'll share a short onboarding runbook link: https://drive.redwood/helixcare/onboarding-runbook (placeholder) and the security pack: https://secure.redwood/security/pack.zip

[08:29] Alex Romero: Ok, any other questions before we recap?

[08:33] Carlos Mendes: One more — sample pricing for the pilot and projected cost for 100k sessions/month? rough order estimate is fine.

[08:42] Alex Romero: I'll include a pilot pricing sheet and a proforma for 50k/100k sessions with Dedicated vs hosted comparisons.

[08:50] Samira Patel: Will the pilot require an NDA before we share PHI-like samples?

[08:56] Alex Romero: We have a standard DPA and can sign an NDA; we'll follow up with legal.

[09:05] Dana Kim: ok thanks — we'll prepare the prompt set and a small eval harness and drop in the shared folder.

[09:12] Priya Nair: Action items recap — I'll capture and send. Next call: perf handoff and infra connection check on 2026-09-23.

[09:22] Marcus Li: I'll start the baseline runs on 9/23 when we have access. Expect a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and token costs.

[09:32] Rita Shah: We'll also include a short doc on recommended batching/quantization toggles for your workload.

[09:40] Alex Romero: Ok wrapping up — thanks everyone. We'll share the items today.

[09:46] Carlos Mendes: Thanks all.

[09:50] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript: occasional auto-caption errors, proper nouns mis-spelled (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" vs Dedicated), some timestamps approximate. Shared references: onboarding runbook link and security pack link above, pricing spreadsheet will be linked in follow up.
